job.title: Local HazMat CDL Driver
job.description:
Disclaimer: SLB completed the acquisition of ChampionX on July 16, 2025. If selected for this position, your employment will begin with ChampionX and will transition to SLB as part of the planned integration.

We have an immediate need for an Operational Specialist in McCook, Nebraska.  If you are a dedicated DOT driving professional with a proven track record of success in customer delivery, we invite you to apply.  This is your opportunity to join a large growing company offering a competitive base hourly rate and benefits. 

What's in it For You:

  • You will join a growing company offering competitive pay and benefits
  • Access to best in class resources, tools, and technology
  • Opportunity for a long term, advanced career path
  • A culture that values safety first, including training and personal protection
  • Comprehensive benefits package (Medical, Dental, Vision, 401K and much more) that starts Day 1
  • $4,000 Hiring Bonus

What You Will Do:

This position will primarily be responsible for providing chemical treatments to oil wells, and the maintenance and safe operation of any type of vehicle used to deliver chemicals to customers, plants and/or warehouse locations.

  • Chemical treating of all scheduled wells and locations on a regular basis
  • Maintain chemical inventory reports
  • Present a professional manner and work closely with salespeople to satisfy customer requirements.
  • Maintain regular communication with sales and supervisor in order to report field problems and/or safety hazards
  • Maintain truck and equipment in a safe and operable condition by performing daily and periodic mechanical and safety inspections
  • Maintain driver's hours of service by using Turnpike and/or paper logbook reporting
  • Keeps current on safety techniques and take advantage of all opportunities to improve driving and safety skills
  • Recognize and avoid safety hazards in the work environment
  • Properly load trucks, prepare daily bills of lading, schedule the order of daily treatments and submit treating reports to sales

Territory / Location Information:

  • This will be a local position that will be based in and will be responsible for chemical treatment and delivery within a 50-mile radius of McCook, NE
  • Candidate must reside within 50 miles of McCook, NE
  • Relief positions also available with a $2.00 an hour travel bonus

Schedule:

  • Multiple Schedules available
  • Monday Thru Friday with an occasional Saturday
  • Weekend rotation availability with days off in the week
  • 10-12 hour day time shifts

Basic/Minimum Qualifications:

  • Minimum high school graduate or GED
  • Must be 21 years of age or older to operate company vehicle
  • Must currently hold a valid Class A or B Commercial Driver's License (CDL), issued by the state in which the candidate resides
  • Must have HazMat and Tanker Endorsements or be willing to be obtain within 30 days
  • One (1) year of commercial driving experience, compliant with Federal Motor Carrier Safety Regulations and DOT regulations, within the past three years required
  • Acceptable motor vehicle record (3 years)
  • All candidates must have the ability to speak, read and write English
  • Immigration sponsorship is not offered for this role
  • Must be comfortable working with cameras in the truck cab
  • No manual transmission restrictions

Physical Demands:

  • Must have the ability to Lift/Carry up to 50 pounds chest high.
  • Must be able to pass a drug screen and physical exam

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Three (3) years commercial driving experience, compliant with Federal Motor Carrier Safety Regulations and DOT regulations, within the past five years required
  • Experience with the operation of forklifts, drum dollies, trailer hoists, chemical pumps, hoses, meters, printers and gauges
  • Experience with handling products in various types of packages including bulk, drums, Porta-Feeds and mini/micro-feed units
  • Knowledge of precautions needed if exposed to H2S (hydrogen sulfide)
  • Experience in customer relations
  • Experience performing warehouse duties, which include preventative maintenance, inventory and ordering of chemicals, receiving incoming shipments, organizing warehouse for safe and efficient chemical storage, operation of customized chemical manufacturing equipment and the upkeep of warehouse grounds
  • Awareness of chemical safety and the measures to take in the event of skin contact or spill

Position Compensation and Benefits

  • Comprehensive benefits package that includes medical, dental, vision, 401(k) with company matching and more!
  • Hourly and overtime pay earning potential between $75,000 to $95,000 a year!

job.title: Warehouse Specialist
job.description:
Disclaimer: SLB completed the acquisition of ChampionX on July 16, 2025. If selected for this position, your employment will begin with ChampionX and will transition to SLB as part of the planned integration.

ChampionX has an immediate need for a Warehouse Specialist located in Williston, ND. If you are a dedicated warehouse operator with a proven track record of success in logistics, we invite you to apply.  This is your opportunity to join a large growing company offering a competitive base hourly rate and benefits. 

What’s in it For You:

·       Access to best-in-class resources, tools, and technology

·       Grow your income as you drive growth

·       Thrive in a company that values a culture of safety to include top-notch safety training and personal protection equipment

·       Comprehensive benefits package starting day 1 of employment- medical, dental, vision, matching 401k and more 

·   Compensation: $24-$26/hr with overtime opportunities.

What You Will Do:

This position will primarily be responsible for loading/unloading products leaving from or arriving at warehouse locations.

·       Report to and receive instructions from the Field Operations Manager

·       Operate necessary equipment such as pumps, mules, forklifts, loading platforms

·       Responsible for making proper hookups from storage tanks to trucks and ensuring the correct chemical is loaded

·       Keep safety areas clear and maintain good housekeeping

·       Load/unload trucks containing drums, bulk totes, and other packaged products

·       Responsible for the sampling of chemicals and related paperwork

·       Perform daily inspection on all equipment used

·       Maintain and monitor in-house mixed chemical bulk totes

·       Pick and stage orders for all upcoming shipments

Basic Qualifications:

·       Minimum high school graduate or GED​

·  Must have a clean MVR

·       No immigration sponsorship offered for this position

·       Must be able to speak, read, and write English

Physical Demands:

·       Must be able to lift and carry a minimum of 50 lbs.

·       Role is deemed safety sensitive and may be subject to employer or customer drug testing

Preferred Qualifications:

·       3 years of experience working in a similar chemical environment

·       Experience with handling products in various types of packages including bulk, drums, bulk totes and mini/micro-feed units

·       Experience performing warehouse duties, which include preventative maintenance duties, inventory and ordering of chemicals, receiving incoming shipments, organizing warehouse for safe and efficient chemical storage, operation of customized chemical manufacturing equipment and the upkeep of warehouse grounds

·       Knowledge of pumps, valves, hand tools, and welding equipment

·       Awareness of chemical safety and the measures to take in the event of skin contact or spill

·       Proficiency with basic Math

·       Basic knowledge of personal computers and Windows software

·       Experience with SAP

What’s in it For You:

  • Join a growing company offering competitive pay
  • Comprehensive benefits package that includes medical, dental, vision, 401(k) with company matching and more
  • Tackle some of the world’s most meaningful challenges including, helping customers achieve clean water, safe food, abundant energy, and healthy environments
  • The ability to shape your career with a company that is passionate about growth
  • Be part of a culture that values its employees and puts safety first
  • Grow your income as you drive growth
  • Opportunity for a long term, advanced career path
  • Access to Employee Resource Groups (ERG’s). These employee-led groups allow employees to come together to explore common interests and foster a diverse and inclusive workplace
  • Access to best-in-class resources, tools, and technology

What You Will Do:

  • Support and engage in our vision of improving lives 
  • Live and be an example of Quartzdyne’s core values: Respect, Grit, Transparency, Honesty, Humility and Accountability 
  • Be a disciple and leader of continuous improvement

Position Details:

  • Performs a wide range of mechanical and electrical maintenance tasks
  • Uses hand and power tools to accomplish these tasks
  • Light repair to machines and facility
  • Light fabrication of metal work and wood work
  • Painting of production equipment and facility
  • Moves production equipment in line changes
  • Changes lubrication and heat transfer fluids in production equipment
  • Maintains fans, compressors, air dryers, and chillers
  • Replaces lighting and ballasts as needed
  • Assists in companywide recycling program of materials and chemicals
  • Drives company vehicle to pick and parts and materials
  • Other maintenance related duties as assigned

Minimum Qualifications:

  • High School Diploma/GED required
  • 2 years experience in general maintenance work
  • Skills using Microsoft Word, PowerPoint and Excel
  • Must be able to drive the company vehicle
  • Valid driver’s license required
  • Immigration sponsorship not offered for this role

Physical Demands:

  • Normal working conditions absent extreme factors 
  • Must be able to see well enough to read reports, send emails, etc.
  • Must be able to hear and speak well enough to communicate with customers and fellow employees 
  • Must be able to lift up to 100lbs periodically
  • Role is deemed safety-sensitive and may be subject to employer or customer drug testing

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Skills in identifying and resolving employee, customer and vendor problems
  • Ability to communicate effectively and professionally with coworkers, customers and vendors both verbally and in writing
  • Ability to work effectively independently and as part of a team
  • Ability to follow oral and written instructions
  • Ability to organize daily activities of self and others
  • Strong desire to learn and be a problem solver
  • Ethical behavior required at all times

Position Compensation and Benefits:

  • Competitive base salaries
  • Medical
  • Dental
  • Vision
  • Employer paid STD and LTD
  • 1X your annual salary of employer paid life insurance
  • 15 days of paid vacation to start
  • 7 days of paid personal leave
  • 12 paid holidays
  • HSA Funding
  • Generous profit sharing
  • 401(k) match up to 6%

ChampionX is now part of SLB, a global technology company driving energy innovation for a balanced planet. As innovators, that’s been our mission for nearly a century.

Quartzdyne, an SLB Company, designs and manufactures precision pressure and temperature transducers for the oil and gas industry. Our proprietary offerings have become the industry standard, elevating how critical data is used to assess the performance of a reservoir and increase oil production. job.title: Account Manager
job.description:
Disclaimer: SLB completed the acquisition of ChampionX on July 16, 2025. If selected for this position, your employment will begin with ChampionX and will transition to SLB as part of the planned integration.

We are looking for an Account Manager located in Bonnyville, AB, area working a regular 5 day – 40 hour work week.  The Account Manager will be primarily responsible for servicing existing programs as well as developing and applying chemical solutions for remediation of customer challenges within targeted accounts in the sales area.

You will be a self starter that has excellent time management skills and a desire to meet customer demands. Strong communication skills are a requirement for this role. In addition, you will be responsible for building long-term relationships throughout your customer base by understanding their key business drivers, executing system assurance programs, and deploying new technologies.

If you have experience as an oilfield operator, as an engineer/engineering technologist or have a proven track record of success in technical sales, we invite you to apply. This is your opportunity to join a large growing company offering a competitive base salary, bonus structure and benefits.

What’s in it For You:

  • Flexible, independent work environment where you will manage a monthly schedule

  • Access to best-in-class resources, tools, and technology

  • Grow your income as you drive growth

  • Thrive in a company that values a culture of safety to include top-notch safety training and personal protection equipment

  • Comprehensive benefits package that includes extended health benefits, a company-paid pension plan, and more!

What You Will Do:

  • Work closely with current and new customers within an assigned territory/customer base.  Understand customer business needs and recommend continuous improvement and innovation plans that will drive customer loyalty.

  • Develop strong relationships with key stakeholders in current and new customer organizations, including plant or facility executives.

  • Generate and execute sales plans in assigned customer base and new customer accounts to meet defined territory profit increase goals.

  • Provide technical support to customers; identifying and resolving customer issues, escalating as required.

  • Engage in problem solving by performing system analysis, interpreting data and providing written recommendations to ensure customer operations are performing at optimal levels.

  • Possible travel within assigned sales territory

Position Details:

  • Candidate must reside within the Lakeland/Bonnyville region.

  • No immigration sponsorship offered.

  • This is a safety sensitive position, and the successful candidate will be required to complete drug and alcohol testing.

  • Must have a valid Driver’s License and acceptable Motor Vehicle Record

Minimum Qualifications:

  • 3 -5 years of technical sales, operating/engineering experience is preferred but not required.

  • High computer application literacy (including Microsoft Office Suite, and ability to learn internal business systems)

  • Prior experience that demonstrates a strong work ethic and ability to multitask

Physical Demands:

  • Must have the ability to Lift/Push/Pull/Carry up to 55 pounds chest high.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience in the oil and gas industry preferred

  • Previous Petrochemical experience

  • Water treatment or specialty chemical industry experience

  • Working knowledge of water treatment systems

  • History of working in a field that required autonomy and self-motivation

  • Prior experience that required excellent communication skills

  • Prior experience that required excellent organizational skills

  • Account leadership experience that includes calling on multilevel plant or facilities management to accomplish company goals

We are looking for a Regional Sales Manager for Windrock to create and execute regional channel strategy for its new line of wireless sensors as it applies to customers and applications. Qualified candidate may reside in Hobbs, NM, Midland, Amarillo or Lubbock, TX.

This is your opportunity to join a global technology company, driving energy innovation for a balanced planet.

  • The ability to make an impact and shape your career with a company that is passionate about growth

  • The support of an organization that believes it is vital to include and engage diverse people, perspectives, and ideas to achieve our best

  • Thrive in a company that values sustainability, drives a safety-focused culture and empowers its employees through continuous improvement

  • Comprehensive benefits package that includes medical, dental, vision, 401(k) company matching and more!

What You Will Do:

Customer Management:

  • Identify customer’s needs, vision cast, and sales opportunities to drive growth

  • Identify and establish business relationships

  • Listen, understand, and convey customer requirements

  • Identify and leverage resources to perform technical / product training for customers at targeted accounts

  • Identify and communicate customer requirements for new products/solutions

Strategy & Planning:

  • Define a regional strategy and implement its execution for years one, two, and three

  • Identify and develop strategic account plans leveraging other channel partner (internal and external) resources

  • Drive sales through direct customer relationships, distributors, and other ChampionX entities

  • Work closely with the organization to ensure that product strategies and performance are meeting growth and Annual Operating Plan targets

  • Work closely with Marketing & Technology teams to understand pros and cons of various solution approaches

Execution:

  • Articulate value story, technology and product positioning to both business and technical users

  • Create incremental demand, opportunities, and close orders

  • Maintain expert level of product and application knowledge within the battery-operated wireless sensor market

  • Meet sales goal targets monthly, quarterly, and yearly

  • Actively manage channel partners effectiveness, prospecting, closing, forecasting, and KPI’s by using a metrics-based approach to report progress and highlight potential roadblocks with proposed mitigation strategies

  • Maintain accurate records of target accounts, opportunities, quotes, projects, contacts and correspondence in company approved databases through our Salesforce CRM

  • Bachelor’s degree in engineering, business, or related field

  • Good overall knowledge of the Oil and Gas Industry

  • 5 years of experience in condition monitoring and wireless sensor applications

  • Self-driven work ethic

  • Strong negotiation skills

  • Excellent communication skills

  • Strong Interpersonal and Organizational skills

  • Strong computer skills, including Microsoft Office suite

  • Competitive attitude and strong work ethic with the ability to enthusiastically represent the company

  • Availability for inter-regional travel as required, 50-70%

Physical Demands

Position Details: This position is located in Sugar Land, Texas.

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Degree in analytical chemistry, materials science, polymer science or related scientific/technical discipline (required, and relevant experience including technology strategy development & implementation, leading & developing teams, and driving innovation. Education and experience should fall in one of the following levels:

    • Bachelors degree and 7 years experience; OR

    • Masters degree and 4 years experience; OR

    • PhD and 2 years experience

  • Five or more years of relevant experiences in management, technology development and innovation areas.

  • Ability to travel up to 20%

Preferred Qualifications:

Physical Demands:

  • Role is deemed safety-sensitive and may be subject to employer or customer drug testing.

  • Medium work:  Exerting up to 50 pounds of force occasionally and/or up to 20 pounds of force frequently, and/or up to 10 pounds of force constantly to move objects.

  • Physical Activities

  • Climbing:  Ascending or descending ladders, stairs, scaffolding, ramps, poles, and the like, using feet and legs and/or hands and arms. Body agility is emphasized.

  • Balancing:  Maintaining body equilibrium to prevent falling when walking, standing, or crouching on narrow, slippery, or erratically moving surfaces.

  • Stooping:  Bending body downward and forward by bending spine at the waist. This factor is important if it occurs to a considerable degree and requires full use of the lower extremities and back muscles.

  • Kneeling:  Bending legs at knee to come to a rest on knees.

  • Crouching:  Bending the body downward and forward by bending leg and spine.

  • Crawling:  Moving about on hands and knees or hands and feet.

  • Reaching:  Extending hand(s) and arm(s) in any direction.

  • Walking:  Moving about on foot to accomplish tasks, particularly for long distances or moving from one work site to another.

  • Pushing:  Using upper extremities to press against something with steady force in order to thrust forward, downward, or outward.

  • Pulling:  Using upper extremities to exert force in order to draw, drag, haul, or tug objects in a sustained motion.

  • Lifting:  Raising objects from a lower to a higher position or moving objects horizontally from position to position.

  • Fingering:  Picking, pinching, typing, or otherwise working, primarily with fingers rather than the whole hand or arm as in handling.

  • Grasping:  Applying pressure to an object with the fingers and palm.

  • Feeling:  Perceiving attributes of objects, such as size, shape, temperature, or texture by touching with skin, particularly that of fingertips.

  • Talking:  Expressing or exchanging ideas by means of the spoken word.  Those activities in which they must convey detailed or important spoken instructions to customer or other workers accurately, loudly, or quickly.

  • Hearing:  Perceiving the nature of sounds at normal speaking levels with or without correction.  Ability to receive detailed information through oral communication, and to make the discriminations in sound.

  • Repetitive motion:  Substantial movement (motions) of the wrists, hands, and/or fingers to use a computer.

  • The employee is required to have close visual acuity to perform an activity such as: visual inspection involving small defects, small parts and/or operation of machines (including inspection), using measurement devices, and/or assembly or fabrication of parts at distances close to the eyes.

  • The employee is required to have visual acuity to operate motor vehicles.

  • The employee is required to have visual acuity to determine the accuracy, neatness, thoroughness of work assigned or to make general observations of facilities or structures.

  • Indoor and outdoor environmental conditions.  Activities occur indoors and outdoors.

  • Extreme heat.  Temperatures above 100 degrees for periods of more than one hour.  Consideration should be given to the effect of other environmental conditions, such as wind and humidity.

  • Hazards.  Includes a variety of physical conditions, such as proximity to moving mechanical parts, moving vehicles, electrical current or exposure to chemicals.

  • Atmospheric conditions.  One or more of the following conditions that affect the respiratory system or the skin:  fumes, odors, dust, mists, gases, or poor ventilation.

  • Oils. There is air and/or skin exposure to oils and other cutting fluids.

  • Preferred Qualifications

job.title: Senior Chemist
job.description:
Job Description

Disclaimer: SLB completed the acquisition of ChampionX on July 16, 2025. If selected for this position, your employment will begin with ChampionX and will transition to SLB as part of the planned integration.

This Senior Chemist position focuses on applying advanced chemical expertise to design and execute laboratory testing, analyze complex data, and support research and development activities. The role requires strong leadership, including opportunities to mentor junior chemists, guiding technical workstreams, and driving best practices in safety, quality, and efficiency, while managing a high-volume workload of up to 1,000 samples per month. Working closely with a small, collaborative team of two other chemists and reporting directly to the Regional Lab Manager, this individual must prioritize teamwork and effective communication to ensure project success. The ideal candidate brings 5+ years of laboratory experience, proven leadership ability, and strong problem-solving skills within a highly team-oriented environment.

The successful candidate will be a technically strong production chemist who thrives in a small-team environment, is comfortable managing a high-volume analytical workload, takes ownership of responsibilities, communicates effectively with customers and colleagues, and contributes positively to a collaborative and accountable laboratory culture.

Minimum Education & Experience Requirements

  • Bachelor's degree in Chemistry or related field with at least 5 years of US Land oilfield production chemistry experience, or
  • Master's degree in Chemistry or related field with at least 3 years of US Land oilfield production chemistry experience
  • Demonstrated experience supporting production chemistry programs for U.S. land-based oil and gas operations.
  • Experience managing high volumes of routine analytical testing while maintaining quality, accuracy, and turnaround time expectations.
  • Proven ability to follow SOPs, work independently, prioritize competing demands, and manage moderately complex projects with minimal supervision.
  • Experience operating and troubleshooting ICP-OES, Ion Chromatography (IC), Gas Chromatography (GC), XRF, or equivalent analytical instrumentation.
  • Strong analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills with exceptional attention to detail.
  • Effective verbal and written communication skills with the ability to communicate technical information to both technical and non-technical audiences.

Required Skills & Experience (Must – Haves)

  • Demonstrated success working within a small laboratory team where collaboration, flexibility, and individual accountability are critical to overall laboratory performance.
  • Demonstrate initiative and ability to work independently and handle multiple tasks
  • Demonstrated ability to adapt to changing priorities while maintaining a strong commitment to safety, quality, and customer responsiveness.
  • Demonstrated desire and initiative to grow into leadership roles over time, including taking on increased responsibility, mentoring peers, and contributing to team development
  • Physically able to lift 50 pounds, climb stairs or ladder, and agile enough to squat and bend over
  • Ability to independently prioritize tasks, manage multiple projects, and meet deadlines with minimal supervision
  • Strong organizational skills and ability to manage a high-volume workload (handling up to 1,000 samples per month)

Preferred Skills & Experience (Nice to Have)

  • 5–10 years of experience in oilfield production chemistry, chemical manufacturing, or industrial analytical laboratory environments.
  •  3+ years of laboratory leadership, technical leadership, mentoring, or senior laboratory experience supporting production chemistry operations.
  •  Demonstrated history of taking ownership of laboratory responsibilities, following through on commitments, and consistently delivering high-quality results.
  • Proven ability to foster a collaborative, respectful, and solutions-oriented work environment through effective communication and constructive engagement with colleagues and stakeholders.
  • Experience presenting technical findings, managing projects, and collaborating effectively across functional teams.
  • Understanding of customer needs and ability to translate analytical data into actionable operational insights.
  • Experience identifying and implementing process improvements that enhance laboratory efficiency, quality, safety, or customer service.

Job Duties:

  • Lead and execute routine and non-routine analytical testing activities in support of customer programs, field operations, and laboratory service commitments.
  • Apply advanced production chemistry knowledge and sound technical judgment to troubleshoot challenges, validate methods, interpret analytical data, and solve complex problems.
  • Support customer programs by designing, conducting, and interpreting laboratory analyses tied to real-world field performance and operational outcomes.
  • Independently manage multiple priorities, project deadlines, customer requests, and stakeholder communications in a fast-paced laboratory environment.
  • Manage high volumes of routine analytical testing while maintaining quality, accuracy, data integrity, and turnaround time expectations.
  • Operate, maintain, troubleshoot, and optimize laboratory instrumentation while ensuring compliance with established QA/QC procedures and laboratory standards.
  • Support the mentoring, training, and development of chemists, technicians, and technologists through coaching, knowledge sharing, and technical guidance.
  • Collaborate with field personnel, sales, technical teams, and customers to translate analytical data into actionable recommendations.
  • Identify opportunities for process improvements that enhance laboratory efficiency, quality, safety, and customer service.
  • Champion safety culture, support continuous improvement initiatives, and contribute positively to overall laboratory performance, efficiency, and team effectiveness.
  • Perform miscellaneous administrative tasks.

job.title: Process Operator
job.description:
Disclaimer: SLB completed the acquisition of ChampionX on July 16, 2025. If selected for this position, your employment will begin with ChampionX and will transition to SLB as part of the planned integration.

We are looking for a Process Operator located in Freeport, Texas. If you are a passionate technical professional who enjoys working in an autonomous, hands-on plant environment and have a proven track record of success, we invite you to apply. This is your opportunity to join a global technology company, driving energy innovation for a balanced planet.

What's In It For You

  • Enjoy paid training while learning from experienced professionals.
  • Opportunity for a long-term, advanced career path in operations, service, sales, or management.
  • Access to best-in-class resources, tools, and technology.
  • Thrive in a company that values sustainability, drives a safety-focused culture, and empowers employees through continuous improvement.
  • Comprehensive benefits package that includes medical, dental, vision, 401(k) with company matching, and more!

What You Will Do

This position is primarily responsible for providing production support to the Freeport, TX plant while maintaining safe operations. This position will require occasional weekend call-outs (including nights and holidays) and will work on a rotating DuPont shift schedule.

Production Operations

  • Be proficient in the use of process equipment.
  • Perform all aspects of manufacturing a product from a process order or bill of material.
  • Operate pumps, valves, scales, and other processing equipment for safe and efficient chemical production.
  • Operate and maintain equipment related to plant utilities and waste treatment.
  • Operate all transporting equipment used to receive raw materials and transport finished products.
  • Effectively load and unload bulk materials from tankers.
  • Make necessary hose line-ups for loading materials from tankers into vessels and vice versa.
  • Prepare drums, pails, totes, and other containers for loading, shipping, and transport of products.
  • Operate scales and maintain the drumming platform.

Production Support and Documentation

  • Operate a computer to perform production functions including generating process orders, inventory checks, label creation, and quality checks.
  • Label and placard packaged materials in accordance with company policy and government regulations.
  • Support processes to meet the requirements of current ISO and Responsible Care standards.
  • Participate in physical inventory activities.
  • May perform required Quality Assurance testing.
  • Be able to act as a second-line Production Planner as needed.

Safety, Environmental, and Equipment Care

  • Maintain a clean, safe, and environmentally compliant work and storage area.
  • Participate in safety meetings and continuous improvement committees.
  • Troubleshoot and repair minor equipment issues and notify maintenance of major repairs.
  • Demonstrate the ability to supervise Assistant Process Operators and Operators.
  • Lead by example through a hands-on approach to safe and efficient operations.
  • Maintain final responsibility for products leaving the plant while supporting a 95% on-time service level.

Pre-Employment Requirements

  • Must successfully complete all pre-employment requirements as applicable.
  • Must be able to meet all site safety requirements.

Position Details

  • Location: Freeport, Texas.
  • Local position based at the Freeport manufacturing plant.
  • Work schedule follows a DuPont rotating shift schedule, including days, nights, weekends, holidays, and overtime as required.
  • Occasional weekend call-outs may be required.

Minimum Qualifications

  • High school diploma or GED.
  • One year of manufacturing experience.
  • Ability to read, write, and speak English.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
  • Team player with the ability to perform physical work.
  • Ability to safely wear a respirator.
  • Ability to wear fall protection when required.
  • Willingness to work weekends.
  • Willingness to work rotating day and night shifts.
  • Ability to lift up to 50 pounds, climb stairs and ladders, squat, bend, and perform physical work throughout the shift.
  • Immigration sponsorship is not offered for this role.

Physical Demands

  • Must have the ability to lift and carry up to 50 pounds, climb stairs and ladders, squat, bend, and perform physically demanding tasks throughout the shift.
  • Role is deemed safety-sensitive and may be subject to employer or customer drug testing.

Working Conditions

  • Work is performed in a chemical manufacturing environment.
  • Exposure to chemicals, noise, heat, humidity, moving equipment, and varying weather conditions.
  • Required use of Personal Protective Equipment (PPE), including respirators, hard hats, safety glasses, gloves, hearing protection, and fall protection as required.
  • Work includes climbing stairs, operating industrial equipment, handling hazardous materials, and working rotating shifts.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Process Technology degree.
  • Transportation experience.
  • Forklift experience.

What’s in it For You:

  • The ability to make an impact and shape your career with a company that is passionate about growth
  • The support of an organization that believes it is vital to include and engage diverse people, perspectives and ideas to achieve our best
  • Thrive in a company that values sustainability, drives a safety-focused culture and has been recognized as one of the most ethical companies in the world
  • Comprehensive benefits package starting day 1 of employment- medical, dental, vision, matching 401k, company paid pension, stock purchase plan, tuition reimbursement and more!

What You Will Do:

  • This position will primarily be responsible for providing safety and limited environmental support to the Odessa Manufacturing Plant.  Position will require occasional weekend /evening call-out in the event on an emergency.
  • Drive Goal Zero culture and initiatives.
  • Conducts safety assessments in the Plant to identify and detect existing or potential risk, incident, and health hazards, determines corrective or preventative measures where indicated, and follows up to ensure measures have been implemented and completed.  These include project JSAs, safe work permits, risk assessments, and PPE assessments, etc.  
  • Ability to educate and train workforce on health, safety and environmental policies and standards as required by company policy, customer requirements and regulatory bodies.
  • Leads or participates in the investigation of near misses, environmental spills and incidents that did or could have resulted in an injury or a release of material to the environment. Work with team to develop Root Cause Analysis (I.e., TapRoot, 5-Why).
  • Performs quarterly IH sampling.   Based on results recommends changes to working conditions to ensure all employees have a safe and healthy working environment.
  • Participates and/or coordinates PSM and RMP program activities including MOC/PSSR meetings, creating and updating operating procedures, and PSM / DHA assessments (What If, HAZOP, etc.)  for covered processes.
  • Participate in Management of Change process and implementation.
  • Ensures compliance with OSHA, NFPA, EPA/TCEQ, DHS, and DOT regulations.  Advanced knowledge of two or more of these regulations is required.
  • Compile and analyze HSE statistics and incident reports. Issue monthly reports to SHE Manager.
  • Preparation of different types of HSE reports as needed in PowerBI / Microsoft Office.
  • Gather data and/or prepare reports / RCA on safety incidents and Process Safety Events
  • Active participation in TPM. 5S Assessment / Audits.
  • Participate in Plant safety / ISO audits and ensure compliance.
  • Execute Continuous Improvement and savings initiatives
  • Partners with employees, management and Front Line Leadership.
  • Implement and maintain company HSE documents adhering to local, state and federal environmental, health and safety regulations.
  • Requires the ability to exercise independent judgment and employ basic reasoning skills.
  • Other duties as required.
  • Maintains confidentiality of all matters.

Basic Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s Degree in Industrial Hygiene, Occupational Safety or other relevant degree with 3 years HSE experience with heavy environmental knowledge or equivalent experience. Professional certification in HSE (ASP, CSP, OHST).
  • Two to four years of relevant experience in manufacturing or field service in the oil and gas industry.

Essential Functions

  • Follow all safety policies and company-wide safety requirements.
  • Encourage action assuring safe behavior.
  • Challenge unsafe behavior and conditions proactively and positively.
  • Regularly and predictably attend work and be punctual.
  • Read, write, and speak English fluently.
  • Use a computer to communicate, create, and access information.
  • Lead safety meetings as needed.
  • Conduct SHE training for employees and contractors.
  • Mentor employees on SHE initiatives and policies.
  • Back up for other plant safety personnel
  • Promote continual improvement within the SHE program.
  • Ability to present to Customers.
  • Ability to work within the US without sponsorship of VISA.

Physical Demands:

  • Must be able to pass a drug screen and physical exam
  • Must have Ability to climb stairs and ladders
  • Must be able to lift and carry 15 lbs regularly and 50 lbs occasionally.
  • Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, peripheral vision, depth perception and ability to adjust focus.
  • The employee is regularly required to talk or hear.
  • The employee is frequently required to use hands to finger, handle, or feel and reach with hands and arms.
  • Employee is required to work in a plant environment which may include inclines, uneven surfaces, and a variety of weather conditions.
  • Employee must be able to regularly bend, stoop, crawl, lay down, twist and push.
  • Employee is required to wear appropriate personal protective equipment including but not limited to shoes/boots, hard hats, safety googles / glass or respirators.

Work Environment:

  • Some work is accomplished indoors and in air conditioned or well-ventilated facilities.
  • Work normally is executed in an office equipped with a telephone and computer.
  • Work will be in a plant environment. This will require frequent visits in the plant a variety of weather and temperature conditions.

Location Information:

  • This will be a local position at the Odessa, TX plant.
  • Day shift
  • Will need to come to plant to attend any emergency / abnormal situations during evening shift / weekends as instructed by HSE Manager.

job.title: Supply Planner
job.description:
Disclaimer: SLB completed the acquisition of ChampionX on July 16, 2025. If selected for this position, your employment will begin with ChampionX and transition to SLB as part of the planned integration.

We are looking for a Supply Planner I located in Sugar Land, Texas. This is your opportunity to join a global technology company, driving energy innovation for a balanced planet.

What’s in it for You

  • Access to best-in-class tools, technology, and continuous learning opportunities
  • A strong safety culture with industry-leading training and personal protective equipment
  • Opportunity to work for a company focused on clean water, safe food, and sustainable energy
  • Company vehicle, fuel card, and cell phone provided (if applicable)
  • Comprehensive benefits package including medical, dental, vision, and 401(k) with company match

What You Will Do:

  • Build strong partnerships with cross-functional teams to support day-to-day supply chain operations.
  • Analyze business trends, customer demand, and planning data to help make informed supply decisions.
  • Use planning systems and data to identify opportunities that improve inventory performance and customer service.
  • Communicate with manufacturing facilities and business partners to help coordinate planning activities across multiple locations.
  • Participate in solving complex supply chain challenges while learning best practices in production and inventory planning.
  • Support continuous improvement initiatives that enhance operational efficiency and strengthen the overall supply chain.
  • Develop your planning, analytical, and problem-solving skills while working in a collaborative, fast-paced environment.
  • Gain exposure to a global manufacturing organization with opportunities for professional growth and career advancement within ChampionX and SLB.

Key Responsibilities

  • Conversion of demand plan into a network supply plan for Family Chemistries.  This includes approving and sending a production plan to manufacturing locations while optimizing network capacity.
  • Identify and resolve forecast accuracy and lead time issues with key stakeholders including Demand Planning, SBUs, and PLMs
  • Balance production planning across the network to maintain sprint capacity, including load leveling in preparation for maintenance shutdowns, seasonal volumes, raw material allocation etc.
  • Identify and resolve capacity constraints over the planning horizon by working with Manufacturing, R&D, Procurement, and the Business Units. 
  • Maintain required inventory levels for Family Chemistries at stocking locations to meet customer service levels.  Implement corrective action when imbalances occur.
  • Regularly monitor and address inactive, slow moving, and excess inventory
  • Coordinate inter-plant scheduling constraints related to schedule break-ins, raw materials, etc. facilitated through regular communication.
  • Lead and implement improvement plans to ensure security of supply for existing and new business
  • Conduct root cause analysis for supply chain issues/constraints/process gaps and drive corrective actions

Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in business, Supply Chain Management, Data Science, or a related subject.
  • Minimum 2 years of relevant experience.
  • Authorization to work in the U.S. without sponsorship
  • High level proficiency with MS Office, primarily Excel
  • Excellent communication, organization, and time management skills

Preferred Qualifications

  • APICS Certification
  • High level of proficiency with common ERP systems, especially JDA Master Planning and SAP (Materials Management (MM), Production Planning (PP))
  • A track record of successfully delivering to Key Performance Indicators and business objectives

ChampionX is now part of SLB, a global technology company driving energy innovation for a balanced planet. For nearly a century, we have focused on unlocking access to energy while advancing sustainability.

job.title: Regional Technical Advisor
job.description:
Disclaimer: SLB completed the acquisition of ChampionX on July 16, 2025. If selected for this position, your employment will begin with ChampionX and will transition to SLB as part of the planned integration.

We are looking for a District Account Manager located in San Antonio, Texas. The District Account Manager will serve as a regional technical advisor to the Eagle Ford commercial team, providing technical expertise and customer support for chemical products and applications. This role leverages a strong foundation in chemical engineering, production chemistry, and process operations to help customers address technical challenges and optimize performance. Working closely with sales representatives and customers, the Specialist evaluates operational requirements, recommends effective chemical treatment solutions, and supports the development of tailored proposals. The position acts as a trusted technical resource throughout the sales process, helping translate complex technical concepts into practical business solutions. Success in this role requires strong problem-solving skills, customer engagement capabilities, and the ability to collaborate across technical and commercial teams. By combining technical knowledge with a customer-focused approach, the Specialist helps drive customer satisfaction, operational reliability, and business growth.

What’s in it For You:

  • You will join a growing company offering competitive pay and benefits

  • Access to best-in-class resources, tools, and technology

  • Opportunity for a long term, advanced career path

  • A culture that values safety first, including training and personal protection

Minimum Education & Experience Requirements:

  • High School Diploma, GED, or equivalent required
  • Minimum 3 years of industry experience
  • Valid driver's license with an acceptable motor vehicle record
  • Ability to travel throughout the assigned sales territory
  • Ability to support up to 10% overnight travel
  • Must be legally authorized to work in the United States (no sponsorship available)

Required Skills & Experience (Must – Haves):

  • 3+ years of experience in chemical applications, production chemicals, technical support, field operations, or a related industry
  • Strong chemical engineering foundation with knowledge of chemical processes, fluid systems, reaction principles, and process design for upstream and midstream operators
  • Competency in corrosion, scale, and other predictive models
  • Strong understanding of production chemistry, chemical treatment programs, and process optimization
  • Familiarity with laboratory testing, product performance evaluations, and field trial execution
  • Understanding of corrosion management, scale control, emulsion treatment, flow assurance, asset integrity, or process improvement initiatives
  • Ability to evaluate operational challenges and recommend practical technical solutions
  • Strong troubleshooting and problem-solving skills with the ability to identify root causes and implement corrective actions
  • Experience supporting customers in field, production, or industrial environments
  • Ability to communicate complex technical concepts to all levels of the customer organization
  • Strong customer service, relationship-building, and interpersonal skills
  • Ability to work collaboratively with sales, operations, laboratory, and technical teams
  • Strong organizational, time management, and project coordination skills
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite and business systems
  • Commitment to safety, compliance, and customer satisfaction

Preferred Skills & Experience (Nice to Have):

  • Bachelor’s degree in Chemical Engineering, Chemistry, Petroleum Engineering, or a related technical discipline
  • Experience supporting commercial sales teams in a technical, pre-sales, or applications engineering capacity
  • Knowledge of production chemicals, water treatment, process treatment, or specialty chemical applications
  • Experience analyzing operational data and translating findings into actionable customer recommendations
  • Experience preparing technical proposals, presentations, and customer-facing reports
  • Demonstrated leadership and mentoring capabilities
  • Ability to conduct technical training sessions for customers and internal stakeholders
  • Knowledge of industry regulations, environmental requirements, and safe chemical handling practices
  • Experience utilizing CRM systems, business intelligence tools, and data visualization platforms
  • Strong project management capabilities with the ability to manage multiple priorities and customer opportunities simultaneously
  • Demonstrated ability to influence customer decisions through technical expertise and consultative problem-solving
  • Experience supporting product development, commercialization, or application testing programs

Job Duties:

  • Serve as the primary technical resource for customers and the commercial team, providing expertise on chemical products, treatment programs, and application recommendations
  • Partner closely with sales representatives to understand customer requirements and develop technically sound solutions that align with operational and business objectives
  • Monitor treatment program performance and recommend adjustments to improve efficiency, reliability, and cost-effectiveness
  • Evaluate customer operations and technical challenges to identify opportunities for process improvement, performance optimization, and reliability enhancement through chemical treatment solutions
  • Provide technical consultation throughout the sales cycle, including opportunity assessment, solution development, proposal support, and post-implementation follow-up
  • Support business growth initiatives by identifying opportunities for expanded product utilization, treatment optimization, and value-added technical services within customer accounts
  • Analyze operational, laboratory, and field performance data to develop recommendations that improve treatment effectiveness, reduce operational risks, and enhance customer outcomes
  • Troubleshoot process and production issues, identify root causes, and recommend appropriate corrective actions
  • Support customer meetings, site visits, technical reviews, field trials, and product evaluations
  • Communicate complex technical concepts in a clear and practical manner to both technical and non-technical stakeholders
  • Deliver technical presentations and training sessions to customers and internal teams as needed
  • Develop and maintain strong customer relationships by serving as a trusted advisor and providing responsive technical support
  • Collaborate with laboratory, operations, engineering, product management, and other cross-functional teams to address customer needs and resolve technical challenges
  • Assist in the preparation of technical reports, proposals, treatment recommendations, performance summaries, and customer presentations
  • Maintain accurate documentation of customer interactions, technical evaluations, project activities, and solution recommendations
  • Stay informed on industry trends, emerging technologies, and competitive solutions to support customer needs and business growth
  • Ensure all activities are conducted in compliance with company policies, customer requirements, and applicable health, safety, environmental, and regulatory standards
  • Promote a strong safety culture and support the safe application, handling, and use of chemical products in the field

job.title: Sr. Chemist
job.description:
Disclaimer: SLB completed the acquisition of ChampionX on July 16, 2025. If selected for this position, your employment will begin with ChampionX and will transition to SLB as part of the planned integration.

This Senior Chemist in Cresson, TX focuses on applying advanced chemical expertise to design and execute laboratory testing, analyze complex data, and support research and development activities. The role requires strong leadership, including opportunities to mentor junior chemists, guiding technical workstreams, and driving best practices in safety, quality, and efficiency, while managing a high-volume workload of up to 1,000 samples per month. Working closely with a small, collaborative team of two other chemists and reporting directly to the Regional Lab Manager, this individual must prioritize teamwork and effective communication to ensure project success. The ideal candidate brings 5+ years of laboratory experience, proven leadership ability, and strong problem-solving skills within a highly team-oriented environment.

The successful candidate will be a technically strong analytical chemist who thrives in a small-team environment, is comfortable managing a high-volume analytical workload, takes ownership of responsibilities, communicates effectively with customers and colleagues, and contributes positively to a collaborative and accountable laboratory culture.

Minimum Education & Experience Requirements

  • Bachelor's degree in Chemistry or related field with at least 3 years of production chemistry experience, or

  • Master's degree in Chemistry or related field with at least 1 years of production chemistry experience

  • Demonstrated experience supporting production chemistry programs for U.S. land-based oil and gas operations.

  • Experience managing high volumes of routine analytical testing while maintaining quality, accuracy, and turnaround time expectations.

  • Proven ability to follow SOPs, work independently, prioritize competing demands, and manage moderately complex projects with minimal supervision.

  • Experience operating and troubleshooting ICP-OES, Ion Chromatography (IC), Gas Chromatography (GC), XRF, or equivalent analytical instrumentation.

  • Proficient in Microsoft Office Suite (Outlook, Excel, PowerPoint, etc) and Laboratory Information Management Systems (LIMS), with experience leveraging data management and reporting tools to support laboratory operations, decision-making, and process improvement.

Required Skills & Experience (Must – Haves)

  • Demonstrated success working within a small laboratory team where collaboration, flexibility, and individual accountability are critical to overall laboratory performance.

  • Demonstrate initiative and ability to work independently and handle multiple tasks.

  • Demonstrated ability to adapt to changing priorities while maintaining a strong commitment to safety, quality, and customer responsiveness.

  • Demonstrated desire and initiative to grow into leadership roles over time, including taking on increased responsibility, mentoring peers, and contributing to team development.

  • Strong analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills with exceptional attention to detail.

  • Effective verbal and written communication skills with the ability to communicate technical information to both technical and non-technical audiences.

  • Physically able to lift 50 pounds, climb stairs or ladder, and agile enough to squat and bend over.

  • Ability to independently prioritize tasks, manage multiple projects, and meet deadlines with minimal supervision.

  • Strong organizational skills and ability to manage a high-volume workload (handling up to 1,000 samples per month).

Preferred Skills & Experience (Nice to Have)

  • 3-5 years of experience in oilfield production chemistry, chemical manufacturing, or industrial analytical laboratory environments.

  •  3+ years of laboratory leadership, technical leadership, mentoring, or senior laboratory experience supporting production chemistry operations.

  •  Demonstrated history of taking ownership of laboratory responsibilities, following through on commitments, and consistently delivering high-quality results.

  • Proven ability to foster a collaborative, respectful, and solutions-oriented work environment through effective communication and constructive engagement with colleagues and stakeholders.

  • Experience presenting technical findings, managing projects, and collaborating effectively across functional teams.

  • Understanding of customer needs and ability to translate analytical data into actionable operational insights.

  • Experience identifying and implementing process improvements that enhance laboratory efficiency, quality, safety, or customer service. 

Job Duties:

  • Lead and execute routine and non-routine analytical testing activities in support of customer programs, field operations, and laboratory service commitments.

  • Apply advanced production chemistry knowledge and sound technical judgment to troubleshoot challenges, validate methods, interpret analytical data, and solve complex problems.

  • Support customer programs by designing, conducting, and interpreting laboratory analyses tied to real-world field performance and operational outcomes.

  • Independently manage multiple priorities, project deadlines, customer requests, and stakeholder communications in a fast-paced laboratory environment.

  • Manage high volumes of routine analytical testing while maintaining quality, accuracy, data integrity, and turnaround time expectations.

  • Operate, maintain, troubleshoot, and optimize laboratory instrumentation while ensuring compliance with established QA/QC procedures and laboratory standards.

  • Support the mentoring, training, and development of chemists, technicians, and technologists through coaching, knowledge sharing, and technical guidance.

  • Collaborate with field personnel, sales, technical teams, and customers to translate analytical data into actionable recommendations.

  • Identify opportunities for process improvements that enhance laboratory efficiency, quality, safety, and customer service.

  • Champion safety culture, support continuous improvement initiatives, and contribute positively to overall laboratory performance, efficiency, and team effectiveness.

  • Perform miscellaneous administrative tasks.

job.title: Local HazMat CDL Driver
job.description:

We have an immediate need for an Operational Specialist in Plainville, KS.  If you are a dedicated DOT driving professional with a proven track record of success in customer delivery, we invite you to apply.  This is your opportunity to join a large growing company offering a competitive base hourly rate and benefits. 

What's in it For You:

  • You will join a growing company offering competitive pay and benefits
  • Access to best in class resources, tools, and technology
  • Opportunity for a long term, advanced career path
  • A culture that values safety first, including training and personal protection
  • Comprehensive benefits package (Medical, Dental, Vision, 401K and much more) that starts Day 1
  • $4,000 Hiring Bonus

What You Will Do:

This position will primarily be responsible for providing chemical treatments to oil wells, and the maintenance and safe operation of any type of vehicle used to deliver chemicals to customers, plants and/or warehouse locations.

  • Chemical treating of all scheduled wells and locations on a regular basis
  • Maintain chemical inventory reports
  • Present a professional manner and work closely with salespeople to satisfy customer requirements.
  • Maintain regular communication with sales and supervisor in order to report field problems and/or safety hazards
  • Maintain truck and equipment in a safe and operable condition by performing daily and periodic mechanical and safety inspections
  • Maintain driver's hours of service by using Turnpike and/or paper logbook reporting
  • Keeps current on safety techniques and take advantage of all opportunities to improve driving and safety skills
  • Recognize and avoid safety hazards in the work environment
  • Properly load trucks, prepare daily bills of lading, schedule the order of daily treatments and submit treating reports to sales

Territory / Location Information:

  • This will be a local position that will be based in and will be responsible for chemical treatment and delivery within a 50-mile radius of McCook, NE
  • Candidate must reside within 50 miles of McCook, NE
  • Relief positions also available with a $2.00 an hour travel bonus

Schedule:

  • Multiple Schedules available
  • Monday Thru Friday with an occasional Saturday
  • Weekend rotation availability with days off in the week
  • 10-12 hour day time shifts

Basic/Minimum Qualifications:

  • Minimum high school graduate or GED
  • Must be 21 years of age or older to operate company vehicle
  • Must currently hold a valid Class A or B Commercial Driver's License (CDL), issued by the state in which the candidate resides
  • Must have HazMat and Tanker Endorsements or be willing to be obtain within 30 days
  • One (1) year of commercial driving experience, compliant with Federal Motor Carrier Safety Regulations and DOT regulations, within the past three years required
  • Acceptable motor vehicle record (3 years)
  • All candidates must have the ability to speak, read and write English
  • Immigration sponsorship is not offered for this role
  • Must be comfortable working with cameras in the truck cab
  • No manual transmission restrictions

Physical Demands:

  • Must have the ability to Lift/Carry up to 50 pounds chest high.
  • Must be able to pass a drug screen and physical exam

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Three (3) years commercial driving experience, compliant with Federal Motor Carrier Safety Regulations and DOT regulations, within the past five years required
  • Experience with the operation of forklifts, drum dollies, trailer hoists, chemical pumps, hoses, meters, printers and gauges
  • Experience with handling products in various types of packages including bulk, drums, Porta-Feeds and mini/micro-feed units
  • Knowledge of precautions needed if exposed to H2S (hydrogen sulfide)
  • Experience in customer relations
  • Experience performing warehouse duties, which include preventative maintenance, inventory and ordering of chemicals, receiving incoming shipments, organizing warehouse for safe and efficient chemical storage, operation of customized chemical manufacturing equipment and the upkeep of warehouse grounds
  • Awareness of chemical safety and the measures to take in the event of skin contact or spill

Position Compensation and Benefits

  • Comprehensive benefits package that includes medical, dental, vision, 401(k) with company matching and more!
  • Hourly and overtime pay earning potential between $80,000 to $95,000 a year!

job.title: Principal Chemist
job.description:
Disclaimer: SLB completed the acquisition of ChampionX on July 16, 2025. If selected for this position, your employment will begin with ChampionX and will transition to SLB as part of the planned integration.

We are seeking a Principal Chemist to join our Production Maximization team in Sugar Land, Texas. In this role, you will provide technical leadership for a global portfolio of production chemistry technologies designed to maximize oil and gas production. You will lead the development and advancement of chemistry solutions for phase separation, water clarification, emulsion resolution, and flow improvement—helping customers improve asset performance, production efficiency, and overall operational reliability.

The ideal candidate brings the ability to turn complex technical challenges into practical, customer-focused solutions. You are an effective communicator, a collaborative partner, and a scientist who thrives in a dynamic, hands-on environment.

If you are passionate about translating chemistry into field-ready production solutions, we encourage you to apply. This is an opportunity to join a growing organization where you can lead innovation, influence product strategy, and deliver measurable value to customers across the energy industry.

What’s in it For You:

  • Make an impact and shape your career with a company committed to growth and innovation.

  • Join an organization that values diverse perspectives, inclusive collaboration, and the power of great teams.

  • Thrive in a company that prioritizes sustainability and fosters a strong safety-first culture.

  • Access a comprehensive benefits package starting on day one, including medical, dental, vision, a matching 401(k), and more.

What You Will Do:

  • Champion a strong safety culture by upholding company standards, promoting best practices, and identifying opportunities for continuous improvement.

  • Lead theoretical and applied research to solve complex production chemistry challenges related to phase separation, emulsion treatment, water clarification, and flow improvement.

  • Drive strategic technology and product development projects with global relevance and meaningful impact on the business.

  • Design and optimize innovative production chemistry formulations that address customer needs and improve field performance.

  • Develop and refine laboratory test methods, screening protocols, and application approaches to evaluate product performance and support successful technology deployment.

  • Interpret experimental and field data, generate actionable insights, and communicate findings through clear technical reports and presentations.

  • Advance continuous improvement across products, processes, and technical workflows to support responsible energy production and long-term business growth.

  • Collaborate across R&D, applications, manufacturing, supply chain, and commercial teams to move technologies from concept through field adoption.

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Degree in Chemistry or a related technical field: Ph.D. or M.S. with 2 years of relevant experience, or B.S. with 4 years of relevant experience.

  • Experience in synthetic chemistry, surface science, or polymer or small-molecule development, supported by strong analytical and characterization capabilities.

  • Understanding structure-property-performance relationships and the ability to apply that knowledge to practical production chemistry challenges.

  • Strong problem-solving skills, including the ability to interpret incomplete data, make sound technical judgments, and drive decisions forward.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Degree in Chemistry or a related technical field: Ph.D. or M.S. with 3+ years of relevant experience, or B.S. with 5+ years of relevant experience.

  • Proven ability to engage with customers, identify technical needs, and translate those needs into differentiated production chemistry solutions.

  • Experience scaling products from laboratory development to pilot and full production, including close collaboration with manufacturing and operations teams.

  • Experience with Design of Experiments, data analytics, or statistical tools to accelerate formulation development and optimize performance is a plus.

  • Strong attention to detail, sound prioritization skills, and the ability to manage multiple priorities effectively.

  • Excellent written, verbal, and visual communication skills, with the ability to communicate effectively across technical, operational, customer, and leadership audiences.

job.title: Senior Staff Scientist
job.description:
Disclaimer: SLB completed the acquisition of ChampionX on July 16, 2025. If selected for this position, employment will begin with ChampionX and will transition to SLB as part of the planned integration.

We are looking for Sr. Staff Scientist / Engineer will support strategic and transformational innovation projects for Production Chemical Technologies within the Technology Production Maximization team located in Sugar Land, Texas. This role is intended for a highly versatile technical expert who communicates effectively, thrives in a collaborative environment, and is comfortable operating autonomously in a hands-on research setting.

The role will advance applied scientific research and product development for Production Maximization product lines, with particular emphasis on emulsion breakers and water clarifiers. The successful candidate will leverage deep expertise in non-ionic surfactants, polymers, interfacial science, colloid and phase behavior, and structure-property relationships to design, formulate, and scale differentiated production chemistry solutions that address complex customer challenges and deliver high-impact innovation.

What You Will Do:

  • Adopt, maintain, and promote safety standards while identifying opportunities for continuous improvement.

  • Conduct applied scientific research to advance technical knowledge and solve complex production challenges related to water clarification and phase separation.

  • Apply fundamental knowledge of synthetic chemistry and interfacial science to formulate new products that meet customer needs.

  • Translate knowledge of non-ionic surfactants, polymers, and interfacial science into emulsion breaker and water clarifier formulations for Production Maximization product lines.

  • Design laboratory screening and performance evaluation strategies that connect formulation variables to oil-water separation, water clarity, emulsion stability, and field applicability.

  • Lead and execute strategic and transformational innovation projects with potential global reach and high business impact.

  • Conduct standardized testing protocols to evaluate product performance, analyze research data, and prepare detailed reports and presentations.

  • Own subject matter expertise for self-initiated research and serve as a technical resource, teacher, and mentor for others.

  • Lead the strategic direction of innovation while collaborating across RD&E teams and business functions.

  • Leverage external technology and collaborations with industry or academia during the innovation process.

  • Steward technical documentation and intellectual property, while monitoring the competitive landscape for disruptive technologies.

  • Work directly with business counterparts and customers to identify needs, translate those needs into technical solutions, and support new technology adoption.

  • Drive continuous improvement of the business to responsibly deliver energy and contribute to a safety-focused, inclusive, and sustainable culture.

Product Line and Science Focus

  • Use structure-property relationships, formulation science, and data-driven experimentation to translate molecular and formulation design into practical field performance.

  • Apply non-ionic surfactant chemistry, polymer science, and interfacial science to understand and manipulate adsorption, wetting, emulsion stability, phase separation, and solids/liquid interface behavior.

  • Develop and expand water clarifier technologies that improve water quality, accelerate separation, and address complex produced-water challenges through new chemistries, blends, and additive strategies.

  • Develop and advance differentiated emulsion breaker technologies for oil-water separation, dehydration, interface control, and field-relevant performance across Production Maximization applications.

Leadership, Culture, and Business Impact

  • Lead innovation with high business impact by applying strategic understanding of global markets, adjacencies, customer needs, and technical gaps to deliver breakthrough solutions.

  • Embody operating principles that reinforce safety, continuous improvement, accountability, collaboration, and inclusive leadership.

  • Build a broad sphere of influence as a safety leader, corporate citizen, mentor, and technical contributor.

  • Grow subject matter expertise through independent learning and by staying current with advances in science and technology.

  • Address personal development opportunities through self-awareness, feedback, mentoring, and engagement with senior leadership.

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Degree in Chemistry, Chemical Engineering, Materials Science, or related technical field. PhD with 9-10+ years of relevant work experience; MS with 12+ years; or BS with 15+ years.

  • Experience with synthetic chemistry and advanced characterization techniques.

  • Strong background in interfacial science, non-ionic surfactant technologies, polymer chemistry, and formulation science relevant to emulsion breaker and water clarifier development.

  • Deep understanding of structure-property relationships and ability to apply them to oil-water separation, water clarification, emulsion stability, and other practical production chemistry challenges.

  • Proven capability developing innovative solutions, including product formulation and development.

  • Ability to work with business counterparts to support customers and enable new technology adoption.

  • Ability to analyze and interpret incomplete information and make sound technical recommendations.

  • Strong record of technical documentation, including reports, presentations, and intellectual property contributions.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Ability to connect and interact with customers to clearly identify needs and translate those needs into solutions.

  • Experience transitioning product development from laboratory scale to pilot and production scale.

  • Experience with formal Design of Experiments and/or data analytics.

  • Detail-oriented work style with excellent time management skills.

  • Excellent written, oral, and visual communication skills, with the ability to communicate effectively at all levels of the organization and with external stakeholders.

  • Recognition as a technical expert, mentor, industry contributor, or trusted technical advisor.

Physical Demands:

  • This role is deemed safety-sensitive and may be subject to employer or customer drug testing.
