job.title: Chemist
job.description:
Disclaimer: SLB completed the acquisition of ChampionX on July 16, 2025. If selected for this position, your employment will begin with ChampionX and will transition to SLB as part of the planned integration.

This Senior Chemist in Cresson, TX focuses on applying advanced chemical expertise to design and execute laboratory testing, analyze complex data, and support research and development activities. The role requires strong leadership, including opportunities to mentor junior chemists, guiding technical workstreams, and driving best practices in safety, quality, and efficiency, while managing a high-volume workload of up to 1,000 samples per month. Working closely with a small, collaborative team of two other chemists and reporting directly to the Regional Lab Manager, this individual must prioritize teamwork and effective communication to ensure project success. The ideal candidate brings 5+ years of laboratory experience, proven leadership ability, and strong problem-solving skills within a highly team-oriented environment.

The successful candidate will be a technically strong analytical chemist who thrives in a small-team environment, is comfortable managing a high-volume analytical workload, takes ownership of responsibilities, communicates effectively with customers and colleagues, and contributes positively to a collaborative and accountable laboratory culture.

Minimum Education & Experience Requirements

  • Bachelor's degree in Chemistry or related field with at least 1+ years of US Land oilfield production chemistry experience, or
  • Master's degree in Chemistry or related field with at least 1 year of US Land oilfield production chemistry experience
  • Demonstrated experience supporting production chemistry programs for U.S. land-based oil and gas operations.
  • Experience managing high volumes of routine analytical testing while maintaining quality, accuracy, and turnaround time expectations.
  • Proven ability to follow SOPs, work independently, prioritize competing demands, and manage moderately complex projects with minimal supervision.
  • Experience operating and troubleshooting ICP-OES, Ion Chromatography (IC), Gas Chromatography (GC), XRF, or equivalent analytical instrumentation.
  • Proficient in Microsoft Office Suite (Outlook, Excel, PowerPoint, etc) and Laboratory Information Management Systems (LIMS), with experience leveraging data management and reporting tools to support laboratory operations, decision-making, and process improvement.

Required Skills & Experience (Must – Haves)

  • Demonstrated success working within a small laboratory team where collaboration, flexibility, and individual accountability are critical to overall laboratory performance.

  • Demonstrate initiative and ability to work independently and handle multiple tasks.

  • Demonstrated ability to adapt to changing priorities while maintaining a strong commitment to safety, quality, and customer responsiveness.

  • Demonstrated desire and initiative to grow into leadership roles over time, including taking on increased responsibility, mentoring peers, and contributing to team development.

  • Strong analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills with exceptional attention to detail.

  • Effective verbal and written communication skills with the ability to communicate technical information to both technical and non-technical audiences.

  • Physically able to lift 50 pounds, climb stairs or ladder, and agile enough to squat and bend over.

  • Ability to independently prioritize tasks, manage multiple projects, and meet deadlines with minimal supervision.

  • Strong organizational skills and ability to manage a high-volume workload (handling up to 1,000 samples per month).

Preferred Skills & Experience (Nice to Have)

  • 3-5 years of experience in oilfield production chemistry, chemical manufacturing, or industrial analytical laboratory environments.

  •  3+ years of laboratory leadership, technical leadership, mentoring, or senior laboratory experience supporting production chemistry operations.

  •  Demonstrated history of taking ownership of laboratory responsibilities, following through on commitments, and consistently delivering high-quality results.

  • Proven ability to foster a collaborative, respectful, and solutions-oriented work environment through effective communication and constructive engagement with colleagues and stakeholders.

  • Experience presenting technical findings, managing projects, and collaborating effectively across functional teams.

  • Understanding of customer needs and ability to translate analytical data into actionable operational insights.

  • Experience identifying and implementing process improvements that enhance laboratory efficiency, quality, safety, or customer service. 

Job Duties:

  • Lead and execute routine and non-routine analytical testing activities in support of customer programs, field operations, and laboratory service commitments.

  • Apply advanced production chemistry knowledge and sound technical judgment to troubleshoot challenges, validate methods, interpret analytical data, and solve complex problems.

  • Support customer programs by designing, conducting, and interpreting laboratory analyses tied to real-world field performance and operational outcomes.

  • Independently manage multiple priorities, project deadlines, customer requests, and stakeholder communications in a fast-paced laboratory environment.

  • Manage high volumes of routine analytical testing while maintaining quality, accuracy, data integrity, and turnaround time expectations.

  • Operate, maintain, troubleshoot, and optimize laboratory instrumentation while ensuring compliance with established QA/QC procedures and laboratory standards.

  • Support the mentoring, training, and development of chemists, technicians, and technologists through coaching, knowledge sharing, and technical guidance.

  • Collaborate with field personnel, sales, technical teams, and customers to translate analytical data into actionable recommendations.

  • Identify opportunities for process improvements that enhance laboratory efficiency, quality, safety, and customer service.

  • Champion safety culture, support continuous improvement initiatives, and contribute positively to overall laboratory performance, efficiency, and team effectiveness.

  • Perform miscellaneous administrative tasks.

job.title: Sensor Operations Analyst
job.description:
Job Description

Disclaimer: SLB completed the acquisition of ChampionX on July 16, 2025. If selected for this position, your employment will begin with ChampionX and will transition to SLB as part of the planned integration.

The Sensor Operations Analyst supports the performance, reliability, and data integrity of a fleet of 12,000+ chemical injection monitoring devices across North America. This role serves as a key liaison between field operations, customers, vendors, and internal teams, providing technical and digital support, troubleshooting device and data issues, monitoring program performance, and driving issue resolution.

The position combines hands-on operational support with data analysis and digital automation tool development, including reporting, automation, and system improvements. The primary focus of this role is the development, implementation, and continuous improvement of digital tools and automation solutions that enhance operational efficiency, improve data visibility, streamline workflows, and support business decision-making. The ideal candidate thrives in a fast-paced environment, balances analytical and operational responsibilities, and collaborates effectively across multiple stakeholders to ensure going program performance.

Minimum Education & Experience Requirements 

  • Bachelor's degree in Science, Engineering, Information Technology, Data Analytics, or a related technical discipline.
  • Minimum 2 years of relevant technical, product support, operations, or data analysis experience.
  • Experience troubleshooting technical systems, devices, software applications, or connectivity issues.
  • Experience working with customers, field personnel, or cross-functional operational teams.

Required Skills & Experience

  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to identify root causes and drive issue resolution.
  • Experience supporting technical products, connected devices, sensors, or digital solutions.
  • Ability to interpret data, monitor performance metrics, and make operational recommendations.
  • Experience troubleshooting device, software, connectivity, and API-related issues.
  • Proficiency with LLMs, AI, and Automation Tools
  • Demonstrated coding knowledge with experience in Python, SQL, and JavaScript
  • Strong customer service and stakeholder management skills.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced, demand-driven environment.
  • Experience creating and maintaining standard operating procedures (SOPs) and delivering user training.
  • Ability to work independently under general supervision and follow established processes and guidelines.
  • Commitment to safety and adherence to company safety procedures.

Preferred Skills & Experience

  • 3 to 5 years of experience combining technical, digital, and operational responsibilities.
  • Experience supporting IoT, remote monitoring, industrial automation, or sensor-based technologies.
  • Python scripting and process automation experience.
  • Experience working with APIs, databases, and system integrations.
  • Knowledge of chemical injection monitoring, production optimization, or oil and gas operations.
  • Experience with device commissioning, configuration, and deployment activities.
  • Experience managing large device fleets and monitoring device health metrics.
  • Training, onboarding, and change management experience.
  • Experience coordinating with vendors, customers, and field service teams.

Job Duties:

  • Develop and maintain automation tools and workflow solutions using Python, APIs, LLMs, and data platforms to streamline processes, improve data accuracy, reduce manual effort, and enhance operational efficiency.
  • Serve as the primary point of contact for field personnel, customers, and internal stakeholders regarding sensor-related questions, issues, and technical support.
  • Provide troubleshooting, user coaching, and issue resolution for sensor devices, software platforms, connectivity challenges, data transmission, and API integrations.
  • Support device commissioning, configuration, deployment, and ongoing maintenance while ensuring data quality and reliability across a fleet of 12,000+ monitoring devices.
  • Monitor device health, pump variance, dosage accuracy, and key performance indicators through exception-based reporting and proactive performance analysis.
  • Develop and maintain Power BI dashboards, performance tracking tools, and reporting solutions to improve operational visibility and decision-making.
  • Create and enhance Python-based automation tools, workflow improvements, API integrations, and data management solutions to increase efficiency, scalability, and program performance.

We are looking for a Business Development Manager located in Houston, TX. The Business Development Manager role plays a fundamental part in ensuring business growth. The role requires a unique combination of strategic thinking and tactical sales execution in a player-coach role. The successful candidate will be an entrepreneurial self-starter who is effective in creating and closing opportunities with minimal supervision. The candidate will have a proven record spanning from regional key account management, strategic channel development, and demand creation. A significant success factor will be the ability to leverage existing ChampionX channels in the region to achieve required business results.

What’s In It For You:

  • The ability to make an impact and shape your career with a company that is passionate about growth.

  • The support of an organization that believes it is vital to include and engage diverse people, perspectives, and ideas to achieve our best.

  • Thrive in a company that values sustainability, drives a safety-focused culture and empowers through continuous improvement.

What You Will Do:

  • Customer Management:

  • Identify customer's needs and sales opportunities to drive growth.

  • Identify and establish business relationships / needs for each target area.

  • Listen, understand, and convey customer requirements.

  • Identify and leverage resources to perform technical / product training for customers at targeted accounts.

  • Identify and communicate customer requirements for new products.

  • Strategy & Planning:

  • Identify and develop strategic account plans leveraging another channel partner (internal and external) resources.

  • Drive sales through direct customer relationships, distributors, and through other ChampionX entities.

  • Work closely with the organization to ensure that product strategies and performance are meeting growth and Annual Operating Plan targets.

  • Work closely with Technology development to understand pros and cons of various technical approaches.

  • Partner and Channel Development:

  • Identify and develop go to market channels for deeper market penetration.

  • Design and deliver effective contracts, collateral and training programs for partners and channels.

  • Execution:

  • Articulate value story, technology, and product positioning to both business and technical users

  • Excellent communication skills that convey conviction and depth in our value proposition.

  • Create incremental demand, opportunities, and close orders.

  • Maintain expert level of product and application knowledge regarding atmospheric sciences.

  • Meet sales goal targets monthly, quarterly, and yearly.

  • Actively manage channel partners effectiveness, prospecting, closing, forecasting, and KPI’s by using a metrics-based approach to report progress and highlight potential roadblocks with proposed mitigation strategies.

  • Maintain accurate records of target accounts, opportunities, quotes, projects, contacts, and correspondence in company approved databases through our Salesforce CRM

  • Other duties as required.

  • Maintains confidentiality of all matters.

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Environmental Engineering, Atmospheric Sciences, Business or related field, minimum of five years’ experience in Oil & Gas segment with strategic connections.

  • Ability to multitask.

  • Strong attention to detail.

  • Exceptional verbal, written, and presentation skills.

  • Ability to work effectively both independently and as part of a team.

  • Practical computer application literacy (including Microsoft Office Suite and ability to learn internal business systems).

  • Salesforce (or other CRM) Experience and Oracle.

  • Ability to work without direct supervision.

  • Collaborative attitude and strong work ethic with the ability to enthusiastically represent the company.

  • Availability for inter-regional trave 60-80%.

  • Service oriented attitude.

  • Strong problem-solving skills and attention to detail

  • Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a team environment

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills

  • Commitment to safety and operational excellence

  • Strong ownership of quality systems and data integrity

  • Proactive troubleshooting and continuous improvement mindset

  • Situational Adaptability

  • Work at times under limited supervision and lead projects with limited scope and complexity

  • Experience in a pilot plant, process development, or scale-up environment

  • Knowledge of SAP for quality data management

job.description:

This is your opportunity to join a global technology company, driving energy innovation for a balanced planet.

What's In It For You

  • Enjoy paid training while learning from experienced professionals.
  • Opportunity for a long-term, advanced career path in operations, service, sales, or management.
  • Access to best-in-class resources, tools, and technology.
  • Thrive in a company that values sustainability, drives a safety-focused culture, and empowers employees through continuous improvement.
  • Comprehensive benefits package that includes medical, dental, vision, 401(k) with company matching, and more!

What You Will Do

This position is primarily responsible for providing production support to the Freeport, TX plant while maintaining safe operations. This position will require occasional weekend call-outs (including nights and holidays) and will work on a rotating DuPont shift schedule.

Production Operations

  • Be proficient in the use of process equipment.
  • Perform all aspects of manufacturing a product from a process order or bill of material.
  • Operate pumps, valves, scales, and other processing equipment for safe and efficient chemical production.
  • Operate and maintain equipment related to plant utilities and waste treatment.
  • Operate all transporting equipment used to receive raw materials and transport finished products.
  • Effectively load and unload bulk materials from tankers.
  • Make necessary hose line-ups for loading materials from tankers into vessels and vice versa.
  • Prepare drums, pails, totes, and other containers for loading, shipping, and transport of products.
  • Operate scales and maintain the drumming platform.

Production Support and Documentation

  • Operate a computer to perform production functions including generating process orders, inventory checks, label creation, and quality checks.
  • Label and placard packaged materials in accordance with company policy and government regulations.
  • Support processes to meet the requirements of current ISO and Responsible Care standards.
  • Participate in physical inventory activities.
  • May perform required Quality Assurance testing.
  • Be able to act as a second-line Production Planner as needed.

Safety, Environmental, and Equipment Care

  • Maintain a clean, safe, and environmentally compliant work and storage area.
  • Participate in safety meetings and continuous improvement committees.
  • Troubleshoot and repair minor equipment issues and notify maintenance of major repairs.
  • Demonstrate the ability to supervise Assistant Process Operators and Operators.
  • Lead by example through a hands-on approach to safe and efficient operations.
  • Maintain final responsibility for products leaving the plant while supporting a 95% on-time service level.

Pre-Employment Requirements

  • Must successfully complete all pre-employment requirements as applicable.
  • Must be able to meet all site safety requirements.

Position Details

  • Location: Freeport, Texas.
  • Local position based at the Freeport manufacturing plant.
  • Work schedule follows a DuPont rotating shift schedule, including days, nights, weekends, holidays, and overtime as required.
  • Occasional weekend call-outs may be required.

Minimum Qualifications

  • High school diploma or GED.
  • One year of manufacturing experience.
  • Ability to read, write, and speak English.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
  • Team player with the ability to perform physical work.
  • Ability to safely wear a respirator.
  • Ability to wear fall protection when required.
  • Willingness to work weekends.
  • Willingness to work rotating day and night shifts.
  • Ability to lift up to 50 pounds, climb stairs and ladders, squat, bend, and perform physical work throughout the shift.
  • Immigration sponsorship is not offered for this role.

Physical Demands

  • Must have the ability to lift and carry up to 50 pounds, climb stairs and ladders, squat, bend, and perform physically demanding tasks throughout the shift.
  • Role is deemed safety-sensitive and may be subject to employer or customer drug testing.

Working Conditions

  • Work is performed in a chemical manufacturing environment.
  • Exposure to chemicals, noise, heat, humidity, moving equipment, and varying weather conditions.
  • Required use of Personal Protective Equipment (PPE), including respirators, hard hats, safety glasses, gloves, hearing protection, and fall protection as required.
  • Work includes climbing stairs, operating industrial equipment, handling hazardous materials, and working rotating shifts.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Process Technology degree.
  • Transportation experience.
  • Forklift experience.

Drive culture of safety; Report safety observations / incidents

job.title: Local HazMat CDL Driver
job.description:
Disclaimer: SLB completed the acquisition of ChampionX on July 16, 2025. If selected for this position, your employment will begin with ChampionX and will transition to SLB as part of the planned integration.

We have an immediate need for an Operational Specialist in Williston, ND.  If you are a dedicated DOT driving professional with a proven track record of success in customer delivery, we invite you to apply.  This is your opportunity to join a large growing company offering a competitive base hourly rate and benefits. 

What's in it For You:

  • You will join a growing company offering competitive pay and benefits
  • Access to best in class resources, tools, and technology
  • Opportunity for a long term, advanced career path
  • A culture that values safety first, including training and personal protection
  • Comprehensive benefits package (Medical, Dental, Vision, 401K and much more) that starts Day 1
  • Starting pay of $28.00 - $30.00 per hour, with incremental wage increases through our Skills Progression Program.
  • $10,000 Hiring Bonus

What You Will Do:

This position will primarily be responsible for providing chemical treatments to oil wells, and the maintenance and safe operation of any type of vehicle used to deliver chemicals to customers, plants and/or warehouse locations.

  • Chemical treating of all scheduled wells and locations on a regular basis
  • Maintain chemical inventory reports
  • Present a professional manner and work closely with salespeople to satisfy customer requirements.
  • Maintain regular communication with sales and supervisor in order to report field problems and/or safety hazards
  • Maintain truck and equipment in a safe and operable condition by performing daily and periodic mechanical and safety inspections
  • Maintain driver's hours of service by using Turnpike and/or paper logbook reporting
  • Keeps current on safety techniques and take advantage of all opportunities to improve driving and safety skills
  • Recognize and avoid safety hazards in the work environment
  • Properly load trucks, prepare daily bills of lading, schedule the order of daily treatments and submit treating reports to sales

Territory / Location Information:

  • This will be a local position that will be based in and will be responsible for chemical treatment and delivery within a 50-mile radius of Williston, ND.
  • Candidate must reside within 50 miles of Williston, ND
  • Relief positions also available with a $2.00 an hour travel bonus

Schedule:

  • Multiple Schedules available
  • Monday Thru Friday with an occasional Saturday
  • Weekend rotation availability with days off in the week
  • 10-12 hour day time shifts

Basic/Minimum Qualifications:

  • Minimum high school graduate or GED
  • Must be 21 years of age or older to operate company vehicle
  • Must currently hold a valid Class A or B Commercial Driver's License (CDL), issued by the state in which the candidate resides
  • Must have HazMat and Tanker Endorsements or be willing to be obtain within 30 days
  • One (1) year of commercial driving experience, compliant with Federal Motor Carrier Safety Regulations and DOT regulations, within the past three years required
  • Acceptable motor vehicle record (3 years)
  • All candidates must have the ability to speak, read and write English
  • Immigration sponsorship is not offered for this role
  • Must be comfortable working with cameras in the truck cab
  • No manual transmission restrictions

Physical Demands:

  • Must have the ability to Lift/Carry up to 50 pounds chest high.
  • Must be able to pass a drug screen and physical exam

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Three (3) years commercial driving experience, compliant with Federal Motor Carrier Safety Regulations and DOT regulations, within the past five years required
  • Experience with the operation of forklifts, drum dollies, trailer hoists, chemical pumps, hoses, meters, printers and gauges
  • Experience with handling products in various types of packages including bulk, drums, Porta-Feeds and mini/micro-feed units
  • Knowledge of precautions needed if exposed to H2S (hydrogen sulfide)
  • Experience in customer relations
  • Experience performing warehouse duties, which include preventative maintenance, inventory and ordering of chemicals, receiving incoming shipments, organizing warehouse for safe and efficient chemical storage, operation of customized chemical manufacturing equipment and the upkeep of warehouse grounds
  • Awareness of chemical safety and the measures to take in the event of skin contact or spill

Position Compensation and Benefits

  • Comprehensive benefits package that includes medical, dental, vision, 401(k) with company matching and more!

  • Investigate and resolve inventory discrepancies, variances, and transaction errors

  • Verify material availability to support manufacturing, assembly, repair, field service, and customer delivery schedules

  • Track serialized equipment and maintain asset traceability throughout the inventory lifecycle

  • Ensure proper storage, handling, and preservation of ESP components to prevent damage and maintain quality standards

  • Collaborate with procurement and supply chain teams regarding material requirements, shortages, and inventory optimization opportunities

  • Prepare inventory reports, performance metrics, and status updates for management

  • Support year-end inventory accounts and financial audits

  • Maintain compliance with company policies, quality management systems, and HSE requirements

  • Identify and implement process improvements to enhance inventory accuracy and operational efficiency

Position Details:

  • 11 days on/3 days off, every other weekend

  • 7:00 p.m. – 7:00 a.m.

Minimum Qualifications:  

  • 1 year of experience in inventory control, warehouse, materials management, or supply chain

  • Ability to drive a forklift

  • Strong attention to detail and commitment to inventory accuracy

  • Strong communication and customer service skills

  • Ability to prioritize and multitask through multiple computer programs

  • Strong proficiency with all Microsoft Office applications; experience with SAP is a plus

  • Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment

  • Highly motivated with a positive attitude and commitment to continuous improvement and operational excellence

  • Problem-solving skills with the ability to identify and resolve shipping and inventory issues

  • Demonstrated ability to work effectively in a team-oriented environment, collaborating with colleagues across departments to achieve shared goals

  • Climbing, balancing, stopping, kneeling, crouching, crawling, reaching, walking, standing, pulling, lifting, grasping, talking, hearing and repetitive motion are all required for this role.

  • Close visual acuity is required for visual inspections involving small defects, small parts and/or operation of machines (including inspection) and motor vehicles, using measurement devices, and/or assembly or fabrication of parts at distances close to the eyes.

• Work modality: Hybrid

• Strong knowledge of direct and indirect taxes, tax compliance, and tax accounting
• Experience with tax reporting, reconciliations, and audits

job.title: Field Service Technician - HPS
job.description:
Disclaimer: SLB completed the acquisition of ChampionX on July 16, 2025. If selected for this position, your employment will begin with ChampionX and will transition to SLB as part of the planned integration.

We are looking for a Field Service Technician to support the Horizontal Pump Systems (HPS) for our Artificial Lift business segment located in Roosevelt, UT. This is your opportunity to join a global technology company, driving energy innovation for a balanced planet.

What's In It For You:

  • Opportunity for a long term, advanced career path

  • A culture that values safety first, including training and personal protection

  • Comprehensive benefits package that includes medical, dental, vision, 401(k) with company matching and more!

What You Will Do:

  • A Horizontal Pump System Technician is responsible for the installation, maintenance, troubleshooting, and repair of horizontal pump systems (HPS) used in industrial, water treatment, oil & gas, and other process environments.

  • This role requires both mechanical and electrical skills to ensure pumps operate efficiently, safely, and in compliance with industry standards.

  • Ensure job deliverables are accurate and delivered on time.

  • Responsible for service delivery execution including installation of horizontal pumps, troubleshooting and perform service inspection.

  • Perform system testing, test pumps for proper flow, pressure and efficiency.

  • Participate in job risk analysis and continual improvement programs.

  • Develop customer contacts to promote company products and services.

  • Ensure company and regulatory standard compliance by implementing the CAT, self-assessments, and well-site inspections.

  • Participate in Service Quality Meetings with customers and improve performance using action plans.

  • Participate in HSE and Quality initiatives.

  • Wear PPE and observe HSE policies.

  • Maintain the required safety training.

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Technical certification or high school diploma/GED

  • 2 years’ experience in field service work

  • 2-year experience with AC/DC motors, SCADA controls and communications systems and/or electrical work.

  • Must have a valid Drivers License

  • Can perform moderately complex pulls and installs independently

  • Strong customer relations skills including the ability to explain and train

  • Knowledge of wiring and cabling

  • Knowledge of proper use of hand tools

  • Strong mechanical and electrical aptitude

  • Strong analytical and problem-solving ability

  • Ability to follow prescribed company policies, procedures, and protocols for installation, service and equipment maintenance

Physical Demands:

  • Work a minimum of 8 hours per day, and available to work overtime as required to meet business needs.

  • Works both in the shop and on-site at customer locations.

  • May be required to drive for long periods of time

  • Operates in industrial or process environments, often outdoors or in confined spaces.

  • Requires ability to work under pressure, including emergency on-call situations

  • Role is deemed safety-sensitive and may be subject to employer or customer drug testing.

  • Exerting up to 50 pounds of force occasionally and/or up to 20 pounds of force frequently, and/or up to 10 pounds of force constantly to move objects.

  • Climbing:  Ascending or descending ladders, stairs, scaffolding, ramps, poles, and the like, using feet and legs and/or hands and arms. Body agility is emphasized.

  • Balancing:  Maintaining body equilibrium to prevent falling when walking, standing, or crouching on narrow, slippery, or erratically moving surfaces.

  • Stooping:  Bending body downward and forward by bending spine at the waist. This factor is important if it occurs to a considerable degree and requires full use of the lower extremities and back muscles.

  • Kneeling:  Bending legs at knee to come to a rest on knees.

  • Crawling:  Moving about on hands and knees or hands and feet.

  • Reaching:  Extending hand(s) and arm(s) in any direction.

  • Walking:  Moving about on foot to accomplish tasks, particularly for long distances or moving from one work site to another.

  • Pushing:  Using upper extremities to press against something with steady force in order to thrust forward, downward, or outward.

  • Pulling:  Using upper extremities to exert force to draw, drag, haul, or tug objects in a sustained motion.

  • Lifting:  Raising objects from a lower to a higher position or moving objects horizontally from position to position.

  • Grasping:  Applying pressure to an object with the fingers and palm.

  • Feeling:  Perceiving attributes of objects, such as size, shape, temperature, or texture by touching with skin, particularly that of fingertips.

  • Talking:  Expressing or exchanging ideas by means of the spoken word.  Those activities in which they must convey detailed or important spoken instructions to customer or other workers accurately, loudly, or quickly.

  • Hearing:  Perceiving the nature of sounds at normal speaking levels with or without correction.  Ability to receive detailed information through oral communication, and to make the discriminations in sound.

  • Repetitive motion:  Substantial movement (motions) of the wrists, hands, and/or fingers to use a computer.

  • The employee is required to have close visual acuity to perform an activity such as: visual inspection involving small defects, small parts and/or operation of machines (including inspection), using measurement devices, and/or assembly or fabrication of parts at distances close to the eyes.

  • The employee is required to have visual acuity to operate motor vehicles.

  • The employee is required to have visual acuity to determine the accuracy, neatness, thoroughness of work assigned or to make general observations of facilities or structures.

  • Indoor and outdoor environmental conditions.  Activities occur indoors and outdoors.

  • Extreme heat.  Temperatures above 100 degrees for periods of more than one hour.  Consideration should be given to the effect of other environmental conditions, such as wind and humidity.

  • Hazards.  Includes a variety of physical conditions, such as proximity to moving mechanical parts, moving vehicles, electrical current or exposure to chemicals.

  • Atmospheric conditions.  One or more of the following conditions that affect the respiratory system or the skin:  fumes, odors, dust, mists, gases, or poor ventilation.

  • Oils. There is air and/or skin exposure to oils and other cutting fluids.

job.title: Fleet Mechanic
job.description:
Disclaimer: SLB completed the acquisition of ChampionX on July 16, 2025. If selected for this position, your employment will begin with ChampionX and will transition to SLB as part of the planned integration.

We have an immediate need for a Fleet Mechanic located in Odessa, TX.  This position is primarily responsible for providing maintenance of any type of heavy duty vehicle used to deliver chemicals to customers, plants, and/or warehouse locations. This is your opportunity to join a large growing company offering a competitive base hourly rate and benefits.   

  

What’s in it For You:  

  • You will join a growing company offering competitive pay and benefits  

  • Access to best-in-class resources, tools, and technology  

  • Opportunity for a long term, advanced career path  

  • A culture that values safety first, including training and personal protection  

  • Comprehensive benefits package (Medical, Dental, Vision, 401K and much more) that starts Day 1  

  

What You Will Do:  

  • Servicing all types of delivery and treating trucks.  

  • Inspect all heavy duty vehicles once a month  

  • Perform scheduled maintenance on all delivery vehicles  

  • Perform field repairs as needed  

  • Take part in planning and scheduling repairs in daily ops meeting  

  • Maintain ChampionX policy inspection maintenance records  

  • Keeps current on safety techniques and take advantage of all opportunities to improve driving and safety skills  

  • Recognize and avoid safety hazards in the work environment  

  • Assist in any emergency that may need mechanical knowledge  

  • Ensure equipment is safe and in proper working order including scheduling of preventative maintenance  

  • Adhere to company policies and follow Standard Operating Procedure per job task  

  • Wear required personal protection equipment (PPE) at all times during job tasks  

  • Ensure a safe work environment, promote a safety culture, and deliver safety training (weekly), etc.  

  • Manage all fleet equipment and maintenance needs  

  • Directing all fleet mechanics and maintenance activities to ensure all repair and maintenance work is performed safely, efficiently, and timely.  

  • Managing monthly OPEX on repair and maintenance  

  • Manage and perform inventory tasks  

  • Ensure all partners in the supply chain are working effectively and efficiently to ensure smooth operations and maintenance.  

   

Position Details:  

  • This position will be based in Odessa, TX. Will require possible travel to locations in the field for repairs.    

   

Minimum Qualifications:  

  • Minimum high school graduate or GED  

  • 2 years diesel mechanic experience  

  • Acceptable motor vehicle record (3 years)  

  • Immigration sponsorship not offered for this role  

   

Physical Demands  

  • Must be able to lift and carry a minimum of 50 lbs.  

  • Role is deemed safety-sensitive and may be subject to employer or customer drug testing  

   

Preferred Qualifications:  

  • 5 years diesel mechanic experience  

  • Chemical pump and plumbing knowledge   

  • Knowledge of vehicle electrical, hydraulic, and chassis systems  

  • Have certifications in brake, CVSA, and A/C systems  

  • Knowledge of use of diagnostic software (ADOC, INSITE)  

  • Experience working on hydraulic pumps, and PTO  

  • Awareness of chemical safety and the measures to take in the event of skin contact or spill  

  • Class A or B Commercial Driver’s License (CDL), issued by the state in which the candidate resides with all the relevant endorsements (X – Hazmat & Tanker)

job.title: Field Service Technician (Hydraulic)
job.description:
Disclaimer: SLB completed the acquisition of ChampionX on July 16, 2025. If selected for this position, your employment will begin with ChampionX and will transition to SLB as part of the planned integration.

We are looking for a Field Service Technician located in Evans, CO. The Pump Mechanic Field Technician is responsible for performing basic to advanced maintenance, new equipment installations, and troubleshooting actions either in the shop or field. This is your opportunity to join a global technology company, driving energy innovation for a balanced planet.

What’s In It For You:

  • Access to best-in-class resources, tools, and technology

  • Opportunity for a long term, advanced career path

  • A culture that values safety first, including training and personal protection

  • Medical, Dental, Vision, 401(k) with up to 6% company match

  • Retirement plans, Group Life, Long-Term, and Short-Term Disability Insurance

  • 11 Paid Holidays, Vacation Time, and 48 hours of Paid Time Off

What You Will Do:

  • Executes the commissioning and decommissioning of multiplex pump skids and components at oil and gas wellsites for use on Jet Pump artificial lift, Salt Water Disposal (SWD) Systems, and other facilities.

  • Perform repairs and troubleshoot multiplex pumps and it’s auxiliary components for operation.  Including but not limited to; electric motor and their variable speed drives (VSD), safety switches, flow meters, various valves, lubrication, and sump pumps.

  • Complete preventative maintenance on the above equipment at regular intervals.

  • Timely and accurately write up service tickets for the customers to review and be invoiced.

  • Develops good working relationships with customers through professional communication.  Respond to customer calls and assist with technical questions.

  • Contributes to the department's continuous improvement culture.

  • Troubleshoot, repair, and service multiplex pumps, commonly known as Triplex’s and Quintuplex’s.

  • Troubleshoot, repair, and service Jet Pump systems used for artificial lift in the oil and gas industry.

  • Responds to customer calls and assist with technical questions.

  • Participate with on-call rotation for the facility, as required by the business.

  • Maintains a clean and well-organized work area and company truck.

Minimum Qualifications:

  • 1 years of experience as a field service mechanic troubleshooting and repairing multiplex pumps and jet pump artificial lift systems.

  • Must have an acceptable driving record per company standards

  • 21 years of age to drive a company vehicle experience

Physical Demands:

  • Must be able to lift and carry 25 lbs regularly and 50 lbs occasionally.

  • Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and ability to adjust focus.

  • The employee is regularly required to talk or hear.

  • The employee is frequently required to use hands to finger, handle, or feel and reach with hands and arms.

  • Employee is required to occasionally walk-in customer field locations which may include inclines, uneven surfaces, and a variety of weather conditions.

  • Employee must be able to regularly bend, stoop, crawl, lay down, twist and push.

  • Employee is required to wear appropriate personal protective equipment including but not limited to shoes/boots, hard hats, or respirators.

  • Work normally is executed at customer field locations in a variety of weather and temperature conditions.

  • Some work is accomplished indoors and in air-conditioned or well-ventilated facilities.

  • Work may include visits to customer offices or field locations.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Basic understanding of downhole pumps and completions.

  • Working knowledge of multi-cylinder engines.

  • Instrumentation & Electrical (I&E) and Automation

Position Compensation and Benefits:

  • Hourly Rate: $24.00 - $26.00 DOE

  • Medical, Dental, Vision, 401(k) with up to 6% company match

  • Retirement plans, Group Life, Long-Term, and Short-Term Disability Insurance

  • 11 Paid Holidays, Vacation Time, and 48 hours of Paid Time Off

In all matters affecting employment, compensation, benefits, working conditions, and opportunities for advancement, we will not discriminate against any employee or applicant for employment because of race, religion, color, creed, national origin, citizenship status, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity and expressions, genetic information, marital status, age, disability, or status as a covered veteran.
